title: The Prom of the quarry
premise: Isandro Whitlock, a nonbinary coder who vents online through an anonymous account, is quietly falling apart when the quarry's legendary ghost begins leaving handwritten notes that use their real name — in ink that shouldn't exist. Following the notes pulls Isandro into a decades-old cover-up: a student who drowned before the quarry's last championship prom, erased from every record. To force the truth into the open, Isandro must win the meaningless robotics championship their school worships and the one that actually matters — a public reckoning at the season's final game, where memory, justice outside the law, and Isandro's own name finally collide.
about_author: Sebastian Montrose is the pen name of a former debate coach who grew up in a mill town with one quarry and too many silences. They write young adult novels about teenagers who refuse to let the past stay politely buried.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet Isandro mid-code at 2 a.m., masking a panic spiral with humor on their anonymous account, 'quarrykid.' At school, the robotics team's championship is treated as the town's only religion. Emotional beat: brittle denial — Isandro insists they're fine while the cracks show in every line.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Taped inside their locker: a note reading 'You dropped something, Isandro Whitlock,' in ink that shimmers like oil on water and won't smudge. No cameras caught anyone. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with a shameful thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: Ghost With Good Handwriting
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with texts from best friend Marisol. Isandro researches the quarry ghost legend — a student who drowned the night of the last championship prom in 1979, scrubbed from yearbooks. Emotional beat: obsession kindling; the legend feels less like a story than a hole.

chapters.title: Teammates and Fault Lines
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The robotics team preps for regionals; captain Dev treats the trophy like a family heirloom. Marisol notices Isandro flinching at their own name during roll call. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by secrets Marisol can sense but not name.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Chemistry-nerd Isandro analyzes the ink: no known pigment, faintly cold to the touch, and it answers heat by darkening — like it's alive. A second note appears: 'They took my name. Don't let them take yours.' Emotional beat: fear tipping into purpose.

chapters.title: The Yearbook That Isn't
chapters.summary: Isandro and Marisol's alternating POV. In the library's sealed archive they find a 1979 yearbook with one photo cut out and a page index that skips a number. Emotional beat: the vertigo of institutional erasure — someone powerful wanted this student gone.

chapters.title: Dev's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev's grandfather coached the '79 team and built the family's reputation on that lost championship. Dev confesses to the reader, not Isandro, that he's found his grandfather's locked trophy case with a name scratched off the plaque. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Notes From the Water
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Notes lead Isandro to the quarry rim at night; the water holds light 'like it's remembering.' They find a student ID badge, waterlogged but legible: R. Vásquez. Emotional beat: the ghost becomes a person, and Isandro stops being afraid of being haunted — they're angry on the ghost's behalf.

chapters.title: Regionals, Barely
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The team scrapes through regionals on a buzzer-beater fix Isandro coded overnight, running on no sleep and too many secrets. Emotional beat: triumph that tastes hollow because Isandro realizes the championship everyone loves was built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Account Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Someone replies to 'quarrykid' with details of Isandro's private posts — the ghost, the badge, things never said aloud. Either the ghost reads the internet, or a living person is steering them. Emotional beat: paranoia; the ground shifts under every certainty.

chapters.title: Rosa Vásquez
chapters.summary: Isandro and Marisol's POV. They find Rosa's sister, now in her sixties, who confirms Rosa drowned the night of the championship prom and the school buried it to protect a beloved coach. Emotional beat: grief across generations; justice was never served, just postponed for fifty years.

chapters.title: What the Trophy Case Keeps
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev opens his grandfather's case and finds Rosa's championship medal hidden beneath false backing — his family's name was bought with her silence. Emotional beat: Dev must choose between legacy and truth, and the chapter ends as he pockets the medal.

chapters.title: Losing on Purpose
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro realizes winning the meaningless robotics championship grants a podium speech at the final game — the one stage the whole town watches. The plan forms: win the one that doesn't matter to expose the one that does. Emotional beat: cold, clarifying resolve.

chapters.title: The Ink Answers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro writes back to the ghost in the same impossible ink (their own tears mixed with quarry water, they discover) and gets a reply: coordinates, a date — the final game — and 'Say my name where they can't cut it out.' Emotional beat: eerie communion; Isandro is no longer alone in this.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Someone tampers with the robot before semifinals; suspicion falls on Isandro, whose anonymous posts have leaked. Marisol defends them publicly, straining her own standing. Emotional beat: friendship tested under fire; Marisol chooses Isandro over safety.

chapters.title: Dev Defects
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev hands Isandro Rosa's medal and his grandfather's coaching ledger, which names the men who covered up the drowning — several still on the school board. Emotional beat: Dev trading his inheritance for a clean conscience; the team becomes a conspiracy of three.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, high-energy. The state robotics final: Isandro's code, Marisol's build, Dev's nerve. They win. Emotional beat: joy, briefly uncomplicated — the last page of Isandro's life before everything changes.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Championship night at the quarry-side stadium; the whole town attends. Isandro takes the podium with the medal, the ledger, and Rosa's name. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into ceremony — a prom, a reckoning, a resurrection of a name.

chapters.title: Say Her Name
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. As Isandro speaks, the stadium lights fail and the impossible ink blazes across the jumbotron: ROSA VÁSQUEZ, 1961–1979. The board's cover-up collapses in real time; the crowd's silence becomes Rosa's applause. Emotional beat: catharsis — justice delivered outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At dawn, the quarry yields Rosa's original championship medal and her cut yearbook photo, which the school must finally hang. The notes stop. Emotional beat: quiet mourning and gratitude; Isandro says goodbye to the ghost who saw them first.

chapters.title: A Name of My Own
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Isandro, emboldened, asks teachers and family to use their chosen name aloud — the same demand Rosa never got to make. Small scenes of correction, support, and one painful refusal. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed as a daily practice, not a single victory.

chapters.title: Prom of the Quarry
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, closing. The school holds its first prom at the restored quarry overlook, renamed for Rosa. Isandro dances with Marisol, Dev toasts the ghost, and the last line of the night is Isandro signing their real name, unafraid, in ordinary ink. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory honored, story complete.
